Area.evidence_source: Mislabeling of distress can lead to tremendous frustration and lead to the use of life-threatening behaviors as a means of communicating intense distress. These behaviors are used as an attempt to prevent fragmentation of care. Several men spoke about feeling that they were in crisis (e.g., suicidal), went to a hospital emergency department, did not feel they were taken seriously, and later resorted to "drastic measures" to demonstrate their current state of crisis. Drastic measures are life-threatening actions that are used to ensure an admission, sometimes after being discharged against the patients' wishes.
